subject: Request: vendor chain mapping and SIG/CAIQ evidence for DataFlow API
messages:

Cc: security_ops@aegishealth.com, procurement@aegishealth.com
Date: 2026-07-19T09:12:34Z
Subject: Vendor chain mapping & evidence needed for DataFlow API

Hi Marissa,

We're kicking off a security review for the DataFlow API integration and need a consolidated package of third-party risk evidence. Can you provide the following by next Monday (26 Jul)?

- Current subprocessor roster (CSV) with roles and access scopes.
- SIG-Lite or CAIQ responses (PDF or spreadsheet).
- Clarification on which subprocessors, if any, have access to in-memory KV caches / runtime caches, and retention TTLs for cached items.
- KMS ownership details (who holds keys, rotation cadence, any HSM/KMS partners).
- SOC 2 attestation (latest) or a link to hosted report.
- Any dataflow diagrams that show cross-border transfers.

We may need to share a subset of these with our internal auditors; please mark anything you consider confidential. If there's a better internal contact to own technical detail (KMS/keys and cache mechanics), loop them in.

Thanks,
Alex Burns
Director, Security Engineering
Aegis Health Systems

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-19T10:03:12Z
Subject: Re: Vendor chain mapping & evidence needed for DataFlow API

Alex — thanks for the clear list. We can get most of this to you within the window. Quick summary below and attachments included: redwood_subprocessor_roster_2026.csv (roster), and a preliminary SIG-Lite PDF. We'll follow up with the full CAIQ and our SOC 2 link next week.

High-level answers:
- Subprocessor roster: attached CSV includes subprocessors, region, and high-level role (compute, storage, telemetry, KMS).
- KV cache access: runtime caches are only accessible to our inference runtime processes on dedicated hosts; no external vendor has direct network access to runtime cache. TTLs vary by workload; default session-level cache is 15 minutes, prefix/KV cache entries are 7 days in default config unless customer pins otherwise.
- KMS: we integrate with customer KMS (BYOK) and use AWS KMS for hosted keys by default; see kms-ownership-matrix.xlsx attached for partners and responsibilities.
- SOC 2: we will provide a secure link to the attestation (we host via our vendor portal).
- Dataflow: attached preliminary dataflow diagram; Grace will produce an annotated EU-dataflow overlay for residency questions.

Jonas is copied to provide the formal technical evidence pack (telemetry, key rotation cadence, and cache isolation descriptions). Grace is copied for data residency diagram. If you'd prefer the evidence delivered to a secure link rather than email attachments, we can post to the Drive link below and flag access controls.

Next steps:
1) Jonas to send the full evidence ZIP (SIG-Lite PDF, CAIQ, SOC2 link, logs sample description).
2) Grace to add a labeled EU-residency layer to the drawio.
3) Marissa to coordinate any DPA amendment with the procurement team.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Alex Burns <alex.burns@aegishealth.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-20T15:22:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Vendor chain mapping & evidence needed for DataFlow API — Technical evidence pack

Alex / team — attaching the technical evidence pack as discussed. Summary of the specific technical items you asked about: 

1) KV cache & runtime access- Our serving runtime maintains ephemeral KV caches on the host filesystem and in RAM. Access model:
   - Only the inference runtime process and local monitoring agents (read-only) access these caches.
   - No remote service or subprocessor can directly query the cache over the network.
   - Cache TTLs: Session cache default = 15 minutes; prefix/KV cache default = 7 days (policy configurable per-customer).

2) Key management and rotation- KMS ownership matrix included (kms-ownership-matrix.xlsx). Key points:
   - Hosted mode: Redwood-managed AWS KMS CMKs; keys rotate automatically via AWS KMS policies.
   - Dedicated/Private: customers can supply BYOK via cloud KMS or HSM.
   - Ephemeral symmetric keys used for internal transport are rotated every 6 hours.
   - Long-lived wrapping keys retained under customer control for BYOK flows.

3) Telemetry, logs, and audit trails- We provide per-request telemetry (token counts, latency, route id) and audit logs for admin actions. Sensitive PII/RAW payloads are redacted in stored telemetry unless explicitly requested under an audit with a lawful basis.

4) Subprocessor privileges- The attached roster categorizes subprocessors into tiers: compute, storage, telemetry, and support. None of the listed subprocessors store customer plaintext models or raw customer input as a persistent store. Role-based access controls are enforced and annually reviewed.

Attachments included in the ZIP posted to Drive: sig-lite-responses-2026.pdf, caiq_responses_2026.xlsx, redwood_subprocessor_roster_2026.csv, dataflow-diagram.drawio, kms-ownership-matrix.xlsx, SOC2_attestation_link.txt (link).

Link to secure evidence bundle: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-example-sig-lite (view-only link, access granted to the three Aegis addresses copied).

If you need a sample of audit log entries (redacted) or a scoped SOC 2 bridge letter for the current quarter, let me know and we can provide it under an NDA.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments referenced: caiq_responses_2026.xlsx, SOC2_attestation_link.txt

- Retention: our policy requires 13 months of admin/audit logs; can you confirm retention is configurable to 13 months and whether export of raw audit logs is available for an on-premise archive?
- DPA amendment: please send a DocuSign link for the minor amendment (we'll need to get it routed to legal).

If these are small clarifications, procurement would like confirmation by COB Fri 2026-07-23.
